claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference with a machine-learned potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will better represent configurational diversity in high-temperature multicomponent HEA liquids.
The proposed method applies to both solid HEAs near melting and fully molten HEAs.
A machine-learning potential can replace the standard EAM reference in a TOR-TILD-like thermodynamic-integration scheme.
The machine-learning reference should be trained on high-fidelity ab initio data sampling liquid-state configurations.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic transition-metal or refractory HEAs such as CoCrFeMnNi.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
HEA liquids near melting exhibit a large diversity of atomic arrangements.
A machine-learning potential provides a better mapping to the ab initio potential-energy surface than an EAM reference.
Better mapping to the ab initio potential-energy surface improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
Conventional EAM potentials are too rigid to capture the range of local atomic arrangements in a high-entropy liquid.
A machine-learning potential trained on ab initio configurations will interpolate more accurately among liquid configurations.
More accurate interpolation will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The intervention could halve the effective thermodynamic-integration error relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Current TOR-TILD EAM references have been shown to be inadequate for representing the many configurations of ab initio HEA liquids.
Insufficient sampling of rare or high-energy configurations in the training database will limit the method.
Alloy-specific electronic effects may lie beyond the capabilities of current machine-learning potentials.
The method's improvement depends strongly on the quality and breadth of its training data.
The hypothesis is falsified if the machine-learning reference reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by less than about 10% relative to the EAM control.
